15: # Forgejo backup retention
16: 
17: ## Overview
18: 
19: Retention decides how many Forgejo dumps are kept and for how long. In this
20: homelab the dumps land on the NAS and are pruned by age, so the policy is the
21: only thing between a full disk and a restorable history.
22: 
23: ## Details
24: 
25: - Keep 7 daily dumps and 4 weekly dumps; older ones are removed by the prune job.
26: - Retention is not controlled by `app.ini` -- the prune step is its own job.
27: - A dump is only useful if it restores, so retention never replaces a restore test.
28:

23: # Forgejo operations — backup, restore, upgrades
24: 
25: ## Overview
26: 
27: Day-to-day operations for a self-hosted Forgejo instance: consistent backups
28: with `forgejo dump` (or snapshotting), safe upgrades between releases, and
29: restore/verification. Forgejo follows semantic versioning since 7.0.0, and the
30: database stores its schema version so a downgrade is refused automatically.
31: 
32: ## Details
33: 
34: ### Backup
35: 
36: The reliable option is a synchronized point-in-time snapshot of all storage
37: Forgejo uses. On k3s that means snapshotting the Longhorn volume
38: (`./02_Knowledge/technologies/kubernetes/longhorn/storage.md`); if storage is
39: spread across several systems (DB on one volume, repos on another), stop
40: Forgejo during the backup so the pieces stay consistent.
41: 
42: For a simple single-filesystem setup the built-in command is:
43: 
44: ```bash
45: forgejo dump
46: ```
47: 
48: - Produces a single zip containing configuration, repositories, and the
49:   database.
50: - SQLite is already included in the zip; for PostgreSQL/MySQL also take a
51:   native `pg_dump`/`mysqldump` — the SQL dump embedded by `forgejo dump` has
52:   known bugs when re-injected into a new database.
53: - Schedule it as a k8s CronJob writing to a backup location (e.g. a separate
54:   volume or object storage), keeping a few rotations.
55: 
56: ### Restore
57: 
58: 1. Stop Forgejo.
59: 2. Extract the dump zip and restore data, repos, and config to the data volume.
60: 3. Restore the native database dump (for Postgres/MySQL).
61: 4. Start Forgejo and verify:
62:    `forgejo doctor check --all --log-file /tmp/doctor.log`
63:    plus a manual web-UI walk-through (login, a repo, an issue).
64: 
65: ### Upgrades
66: 
67: Forgejo release lifecycle:
68: 
69: | Channel | Support |
70: |---|---|
71: | **Stable** (latest) | Bugfix + security fixes for ~3 months + 2-week overlap |
72: | **LTS** (version published the first quarter of every year) | Critical fixes for ~1 year 3 months |
73: | **Experimental** (dev) | Not for production |
74: 
75: Upgrade procedure:
76: 
77: 1. **Back up first** — required when moving across a stable release, wise for
78:    minor/patch.
79: 2. Read the release notes for the target version, including known problematic
80:    upgrade paths (see the upgrade guide).
81: 3. Before switching: `forgejo manager flush-queues` (queued data is not
82:    guaranteed compatible between versions).
83: 4. Perform the upgrade by replacing the container image or binary — migrations
84:    run automatically on first start.
85: 5. **Verify carefully**: `forgejo doctor check --all` plus a manual checklist.
86:    A restore after an upgrade is easy; fixing a live instance weeks later is not.
87: 
88: Notes:
89: 
90: - Major version jumps (e.g. 15 → 16) may contain breaking changes and require
91:   the manual procedure; upgrading X → X+1 needs human verification. Staying on
92:   the `16` image tag gives minor updates automatically.
93: - Docker installs need docker >= 20.10.6.
94: - The database version guard refuses to start a downgraded binary against a
95:   newer database — do not bypass it.
96: - Subscribe to the security-announcements repo to plan security releases.
97: 
98: ### Day-to-day
99: 
100: - Logs: k8s — `kubectl logs -f deploy/forgejo -n forgejo`; Forgejo can also
101:   write logs to files via `[log]` sections (console/file modes); SQL logging
102:   is toggled by `LOG_SQL=true` in the `[database]` section.
103: - Health: rely on pod liveness/readiness probes hitting the web port; run
104:   `forgejo doctor` after any upgrade.
105: - Cross-check storage usage on the Longhorn PVC periodically.
106: 
107: ## Sources / Further Reading
108: 
109: - Upgrade guide: https://forgejo.org/docs/latest/admin/upgrade/
110: - CLI reference (`dump`, `doctor`, `forgejo-cli`): https://forgejo.org/docs/latest/admin/command-line/
111: - Release schedule: https://forgejo.org/docs/latest/admin/release-schedule/
112: - Logging configuration: https://forgejo.org/docs/latest/admin/troubleshooting/logging/
113: - Install: `./02_Knowledge/technologies/services/forgejo/install-config.md`

# Backups and Backup Restoration

As your Forgejo installation becomes a critical part of your development lifecycle, the data within it needs to be saved in a backup in order to ensure you don’t lose anything.

Forgejo doesn’t provide or recommend any specific backup tool, but does provide information on what needs to be backed up, how to manage a backup cycle, and how to restore Forgejo to working order from a backup.

## Backing Up Forgejo[](#backing-up-forgejo)

Warning

It is strongly recommended to **shut down** Forgejo during a backup.

Forgejo saves data in multiple different systems, even in its simplest configuration: Git repositories and bulk files are saved on disk as regular files, and a SQL database is used to record information about user interactions. It is not trivial to perform a consistent backup of all that data while Forgejo is running. An inconsistent backup may result in data loss when attempting to restore it.

### Database[](#database)

For SQLite, the database file in the config option [`[database].PATH`](../../config-cheat-sheet/#database-database) needs to be backed up with any file backup tool.

For other databases, use database backup tools that are appropriate to your [selected database engine](../../installation/database-preparation/) to create a backup of the Forgejo SQL database. Any tool designed to work with that database engine should work with Forgejo.

- MariaDB: [mariadb-backup](https://mariadb.com/docs/server/server-usage/backup-and-restore/mariadb-backup/full-backup-and-restore-with-mariadb-backup)

- MySQL: [mysql](https://dev.mysql.com/doc/refman/8.4/en/mysqldump.html)

- PostgreSQL [pg\_dump](https://www.postgresql.org/docs/current/app-pgdump.html)

Note

With a SQLite database and a default configuration, backing up the `data` folder covers the requirements described in the *Database*, *Repositories*, *Storage*, *Queues*, and *Indexer* sections.

### Repositories[](#repositories)

Forgejo’s repositories are stored on disk. By default, they are in the directory `data` in Forgejo’s [`WORK_PATH`](../../config-cheat-sheet/#overall-default), in a subdirectory `forgejo-repositories`. This configuration may be changed with either [`[server].APP_DATA_PATH`](../../config-cheat-sheet/#server-server) or [`[repository].ROOT`](../../config-cheat-sheet/#repository-repository).

Once you’ve identified the correct folder, you may use any file backup tool to backup this folder when Forgejo is offline.

### Storage[](#storage)

Forgejo’s [storage subsystem](../storage/) is used for the storage of larger files. Each supported subsystem can be configured to store data in local files (called `local`), or in an S3-compatible object storage system (called `minio`).

If using `local` storage, then backing up Forgejo must include all the configured [subsystem directories](../../config-cheat-sheet/#storage.storage). By default, all of these paths are under the directory `data` in Forgejo’s [`WORK_PATH`](../../config-cheat-sheet/#overall-default), but this can be overridden with [`[server].APP_DATA_PATH`](../../config-cheat-sheet/#server-server), or individually on each storage subsystem. Check that every expected path in the [storage subsystem](../storage/) list is in your backup, if they’re applicable to your installation. You may use any file backup tool to backup the locations when Forgejo is offline.

If using `minio` storage, then you should make sure that the remote storage system has appropriate backups, or use a backup tool to keep a copy of the stored artifacts.

### Queues[](#queues)

Background work that is queued but has not yet been executed is stored in a configurable queuing system, defined by the config settings under the [`[queue]`](../../config-cheat-sheet/#queue-queue-and-queue) section. If this data is lost, then queued work will never be completed, which will cause system inconsistencies. These inconsistencies would generally recover over time as new background work replaces the lost work.

If the `[queue].TYPE` setting is `level`, which is the default value, then by default the queues are in the directory `data` in Forgejo’s [`WORK_PATH`](../../config-cheat-sheet/#overall-default), in a subdirectory `queues`. This configuration may be changed with either [`[server].APP_DATA_PATH`](../../config-cheat-sheet/#server-server) or [`[queue].DATADIR`](../../config-cheat-sheet/#queue-queue-and-queue). You may use any file backup tool to backup the locations when Forgejo is offline.

If the `[queue].TYPE` setting is `redis`, then ensure the connected redis server implementation is persistent (not in-memory only), and is backed up.

For the `[queue].TYPE` of `channel` or `dummy`, no backups are possible. Queued background work will be lost when Forgejo is shutdown.

### Configuration Settings[](#configuration-settings)

The Forgejo configuration file, `app.ini`, contains a few critical values that must be backed up in order to restore an instance later. It is recommended that the **entire file is backed up**, but pay specific notice to these configuration settings which contain unique, non-reproducible information:

- [`[security].SECRET_KEY`](../../config-cheat-sheet/#security-security), or the file located at `[security].SECRET_KEY_URI`: some values are encrypted in Forgejo’s database using this key. If it is not preserved between a backup and a restore, then Forgejo will not be able to access the encrypted values. This will break credentials stored in Forgejo, such as webhook credentials, Forgejo Actions secrets, repository mirroring credentials, two-factor authentication configurations, and possibly more in the future.

- [`[oauth2].JWT_SECRET`](../../config-cheat-sheet/#oauth2-oauth2), or the file located at `[oauth2].JWT_SECRET_URI`: OAuth credentials generated by Forgejo are encrypted or signed with this key. If it is not preserved between a backup and a restore, then systems integrating with Forgejo will need to reauthenticate.

- If using `[server].START_SSH_SERVER = true`, the file located at [`[server].SSH_SERVER_HOST_KEYS`](../../config-cheat-sheet/#server-server) and its associated `{...}.pub` file should be included in a backup. If they are not preserved between a backup and a restore, then SSH clients attempting to connect to the Forgejo host will receive SSH host key validation errors. If remote automated mirrors or CI systems are accessing Forgejo, such errors can be tricky to resolve as the host key validity may be saved on first connect, and be difficult or impossible to revalidate.

### Indexers[](#indexers)

Indexers provide the ability to search issues, or search repository code. If the data related to them is lost, then it can be rebuilt, but it may be time-consuming or I/O intensive. Backing it up is recommended for large installations.

#### Issue Indexer[](#issue-indexer)

If the [`[indexer].ISSUE_INDEXER_TYPE`](../../config-cheat-sheet/#indexer-indexer) setting is `bleve`, which is the default value, then bleve data by default is in the directory `data` in Forgejo’s [`WORK_PATH`](../../config-cheat-sheet/#overall-default), in a subdirectory `indexers`. This configuration may be changed with either [`[server].APP_DATA_PATH`](../../config-cheat-sheet/#server-server) or [`[indexer].ISSUE_INDEXER_PATH`](../../config-cheat-sheet/#indexer-indexer). You may use any file backup tool to backup the locations when Forgejo is offline.

If `[indexer].ISSUE_INDEXER_TYPE` is `db`, then the database is used for issue searches. No additional data must be backed up.

If `[indexer].ISSUE_INDEXER_TYPE` is `elasticsearch` or `meilisearch`, then the connected search engine should be backed up independently of Forgejo.

#### Repository Indexer[](#repository-indexer)

If [`[indexer].REPO_INDEXER_ENABLED`](../../config-cheat-sheet/#indexer-indexer) is set to `true`, then repository code indexing will occur and that data may be backed up. If not, this section can be skipped.

If the [`[indexer].REPO_INDEXER_TYPE`](../../config-cheat-sheet/#indexer-indexer) setting is `bleve`, which is the default value, or `zoekt`, then index data by default is in the directory `data` in Forgejo’s [`WORK_PATH`](../../config-cheat-sheet/#overall-default), in a subdirectory `indexers`. This configuration may be changed with either [`[server].APP_DATA_PATH`](../../config-cheat-sheet/#server-server) or [`[indexer].REPO_INDEXER_PATH`](../../config-cheat-sheet/#indexer-indexer). You may use any file backup tool to backup the locations when Forgejo is offline.

If `[indexer].REPO_INDEXER_TYPE` is `elasticsearch`, then the connected search engine should be backed up independently of Forgejo.

### Logs[](#logs)

It is not necessary to backup Forgejo’s logs. However, you may choose to do so if they are used routinely for log analysis, or may form an important chain analyzing a security incident in the future.

If [`[log].MODE`](../../config-cheat-sheet/#log-log) is set to `file`, then `[log].ROOT_PATH` will contain Forgejo’s server logs. You may use any file backup tool to backup this location when Forgejo is offline.

If [`[log].MODE`](../../config-cheat-sheet/#log-log) is set to `console`, then Forgejo’s logs are provided to another system (for example, systemd, or docker). Backing up these logs would require specific knowledge of the external system.

## Restoring Forgejo[](#restoring-forgejo)

Restoring Forgejo from a backup requires coordinating the knowledge of how it was backed up, what tools were used to back it up, and what configuration options were in-use in Forgejo.

In general:

- Restore Forgejo’s database, using the appropriate database-specific tool, or file-based tool if using SQLite.

- Restore files, as they were backed up. Typically this is as simple as restoring a `data` directory, which is the parent of all the default file locations. The file locations are described above: [Repositories](#repositories), [Storage](#storage), [Queues](#queues), and [Indexers](#indexers).

- Restore the [app.ini config file](#configuration-settings), or rebuild it if necessary pointing to new restored file paths.

- Start-up Forgejo.

After successfully starting Forgejo and logging in as an administrator, these maintenance tasks can be useful to ensure the Forgejo instance is fully operational after a restore. From the `/admin/monitor/cron` admin management page:

- If using SSH: Regenerate Forgejo SSH keys and SSH principals by running the “Update the “.ssh/authorized\_keys” file with Forgejo SSH keys” and “Update the “.ssh/authorized\_principals” file with Forgejo SSH principals” cron jobs. These files were not included in the backup procedures described as all the data in the database is authoritative and these files can be recreated easily.

- If you did not backup, or restore, the [issue indexer](#issue-indexer): Rebuild the issue index by running the “Rebuild issue indexer” cron job.

- If you did not backup, or restore, the [repository indexer](#repository-indexer), it will rebuild automatically on Forgejo startup.

# Backups and Backup Restoration

As your Forgejo installation becomes a critical part of your development lifecycle, the data within it needs to be saved in a backup in order to ensure you don’t lose anything.

Forgejo doesn’t provide or recommend any specific backup tool, but does provide information on what needs to be backed up, how to manage a backup cycle, and how to restore Forgejo to working order from a backup.

## Backing Up Forgejo[](#backing-up-forgejo)

Warning

It is strongly recommended to **shut down** Forgejo during a backup.

Forgejo saves data in multiple different systems, even in its simplest configuration: Git repositories and bulk files are saved on disk as regular files, and a SQL database is used to record information about user interactions. It is not trivial to perform a consistent backup of all that data while Forgejo is running. An inconsistent backup may result in data loss when attempting to restore it.

### Database[](#database)

For SQLite, the database file in the config option [`[database].PATH`](../../config-cheat-sheet/#database-database) needs to be backed up with any file backup tool.

For other databases, use database backup tools that are appropriate to your [selected database engine](../../installation/database-preparation/) to create a backup of the Forgejo SQL database. Any tool designed to work with that database engine should work with Forgejo.

- MariaDB: [mariadb-backup](https://mariadb.com/docs/server/server-usage/backup-and-restore/mariadb-backup/full-backup-and-restore-with-mariadb-backup)

- MySQL: [mysql](https://dev.mysql.com/doc/refman/8.4/en/mysqldump.html)

- PostgreSQL [pg\_dump](https://www.postgresql.org/docs/current/app-pgdump.html)

Note

With a SQLite database and a default configuration, backing up the `data` folder covers the requirements described in the *Database*, *Repositories*, *Storage*, *Queues*, and *Indexer* sections.

### Repositories[](#repositories)

Forgejo’s repositories are stored on disk. By default, they are in the directory `data` in Forgejo’s [`WORK_PATH`](../../config-cheat-sheet/#overall-default), in a subdirectory `forgejo-repositories`. This configuration may be changed with either [`[server].APP_DATA_PATH`](../../config-cheat-sheet/#server-server) or [`[repository].ROOT`](../../config-cheat-sheet/#repository-repository).

Once you’ve identified the correct folder, you may use any file backup tool to backup this folder when Forgejo is offline.

### Storage[](#storage)

Forgejo’s [storage subsystem](../storage/) is used for the storage of larger files. Each supported subsystem can be configured to store data in local files (called `local`), or in an S3-compatible object storage system (called `minio`).

If using `local` storage, then backing up Forgejo must include all the configured [subsystem directories](../../config-cheat-sheet/#storage.storage). By default, all of these paths are under the directory `data` in Forgejo’s [`WORK_PATH`](../../config-cheat-sheet/#overall-default), but this can be overridden with [`[server].APP_DATA_PATH`](../../config-cheat-sheet/#server-server), or individually on each storage subsystem. Check that every expected path in the [storage subsystem](../storage/) list is in your backup, if they’re applicable to your installation. You may use any file backup tool to backup the locations when Forgejo is offline.

If using `minio` storage, then you should make sure that the remote storage system has appropriate backups, or use a backup tool to keep a copy of the stored artifacts.

### Queues[](#queues)

Background work that is queued but has not yet been executed is stored in a configurable queuing system, defined by the config settings under the [`[queue]`](../../config-cheat-sheet/#queue-queue-and-queue) section. If this data is lost, then queued work will never be completed, which will cause system inconsistencies. These inconsistencies would generally recover over time as new background work replaces the lost work.

If the `[queue].TYPE` setting is `level`, which is the default value, then by default the queues are in the directory `data` in Forgejo’s [`WORK_PATH`](../../config-cheat-sheet/#overall-default), in a subdirectory `queues`. This configuration may be changed with either [`[server].APP_DATA_PATH`](../../config-cheat-sheet/#server-server) or [`[queue].DATADIR`](../../config-cheat-sheet/#queue-queue-and-queue). You may use any file backup tool to backup the locations when Forgejo is offline.

If the `[queue].TYPE` setting is `redis`, then ensure the connected redis server implementation is persistent (not in-memory only), and is backed up.

For the `[queue].TYPE` of `channel` or `dummy`, no backups are possible. Queued background work will be lost when Forgejo is shutdown.

### Configuration Settings[](#configuration-settings)

The Forgejo configuration file, `app.ini`, contains a few critical values that must be backed up in order to restore an instance later. It is recommended that the **entire file is backed up**, but pay specific notice to these configuration settings which contain unique, non-reproducible information:

- [`[security].SECRET_KEY`](../../config-cheat-sheet/#security-security), or the file located at `[security].SECRET_KEY_URI`: some values are encrypted in Forgejo’s database using this key. If it is not preserved between a backup and a restore, then Forgejo will not be able to access the encrypted values. This will break credentials stored in Forgejo, such as webhook credentials, Forgejo Actions secrets, repository mirroring credentials, two-factor authentication configurations, and possibly more in the future.

- [`[oauth2].JWT_SECRET`](../../config-cheat-sheet/#oauth2-oauth2), or the file located at `[oauth2].JWT_SECRET_URI`: OAuth credentials generated by Forgejo are encrypted or signed with this key. If it is not preserved between a backup and a restore, then systems integrating with Forgejo will need to reauthenticate.

- If using `[server].START_SSH_SERVER = true`, the file located at [`[server].SSH_SERVER_HOST_KEYS`](../../config-cheat-sheet/#server-server) and its associated `{...}.pub` file should be included in a backup. If they are not preserved between a backup and a restore, then SSH clients attempting to connect to the Forgejo host will receive SSH host key validation errors. If remote automated mirrors or CI systems are accessing Forgejo, such errors can be tricky to resolve as the host key validity may be saved on first connect, and be difficult or impossible to revalidate.

### Indexers[](#indexers)

Indexers provide the ability to search issues, or search repository code. If the data related to them is lost, then it can be rebuilt, but it may be time-consuming or I/O intensive. Backing it up is recommended for large installations.

#### Issue Indexer[](#issue-indexer)

If the [`[indexer].ISSUE_INDEXER_TYPE`](../../config-cheat-sheet/#indexer-indexer) setting is `bleve`, which is the default value, then bleve data by default is in the directory `data` in Forgejo’s [`WORK_PATH`](../../config-cheat-sheet/#overall-default), in a subdirectory `indexers`. This configuration may be changed with either [`[server].APP_DATA_PATH`](../../config-cheat-sheet/#server-server) or [`[indexer].ISSUE_INDEXER_PATH`](../../config-cheat-sheet/#indexer-indexer). You may use any file backup tool to backup the locations when Forgejo is offline.

If `[indexer].ISSUE_INDEXER_TYPE` is `db`, then the database is used for issue searches. No additional data must be backed up.

If `[indexer].ISSUE_INDEXER_TYPE` is `elasticsearch` or `meilisearch`, then the connected search engine should be backed up independently of Forgejo.

#### Repository Indexer[](#repository-indexer)

If [`[indexer].REPO_INDEXER_ENABLED`](../../config-cheat-sheet/#indexer-indexer) is set to `true`, then repository code indexing will occur and that data may be backed up. If not, this section can be skipped.

If the [`[indexer].REPO_INDEXER_TYPE`](../../config-cheat-sheet/#indexer-indexer) setting is `bleve`, which is the default value, or `zoekt`, then index data by default is in the directory `data` in Forgejo’s [`WORK_PATH`](../../config-cheat-sheet/#overall-default), in a subdirectory `indexers`. This configuration may be changed with either [`[server].APP_DATA_PATH`](../../config-cheat-sheet/#server-server) or [`[indexer].REPO_INDEXER_PATH`](../../config-cheat-sheet/#indexer-indexer). You may use any file backup tool to backup the locations when Forgejo is offline.

If `[indexer].REPO_INDEXER_TYPE` is `elasticsearch`, then the connected search engine should be backed up independently of Forgejo.

### Logs[](#logs)

It is not necessary to backup Forgejo’s logs. However, you may choose to do so if they are used routinely for log analysis, or may form an important chain analyzing a security incident in the future.

If [`[log].MODE`](../../config-cheat-sheet/#log-log) is set to `file`, then `[log].ROOT_PATH` will contain Forgejo’s server logs. You may use any file backup tool to backup this location when Forgejo is offline.

If [`[log].MODE`](../../config-cheat-sheet/#log-log) is set to `console`, then Forgejo’s logs are provided to another system (for example, systemd, or docker). Backing up these logs would require specific knowledge of the external system.

## Restoring Forgejo[](#restoring-forgejo)

Restoring Forgejo from a backup requires coordinating the knowledge of how it was backed up, what tools were used to back it up, and what configuration options were in-use in Forgejo.

In general:

- Restore Forgejo’s database, using the appropriate database-specific tool, or file-based tool if using SQLite.

- Restore files, as they were backed up. Typically this is as simple as restoring a `data` directory, which is the parent of all the default file locations. The file locations are described above: [Repositories](#repositories), [Storage](#storage), [Queues](#queues), and [Indexers](#indexers).

- Restore the [app.ini config file](#configuration-settings), or rebuild it if necessary pointing to new restored file paths.

- Start-up Forgejo.

After successfully starting Forgejo and logging in as an administrator, these maintenance tasks can be useful to ensure the Forgejo instance is fully operational after a restore. From the `/admin/monitor/cron` admin management page:

- If using SSH: Regenerate Forgejo SSH keys and SSH principals by running the “Update the “.ssh/authorized\_keys” file with Forgejo SSH keys” and “Update the “.ssh/authorized\_principals” file with Forgejo SSH principals” cron jobs. These files were not included in the backup procedures described as all the data in the database is authoritative and these files can be recreated easily.

- If you did not backup, or restore, the [issue indexer](#issue-indexer): Rebuild the issue index by running the “Rebuild issue indexer” cron job.

- If you did not backup, or restore, the [repository indexer](#repository-indexer), it will rebuild automatically on Forgejo startup.
